newsitem.title: PERU: Tremors hamper rescue of Peruvian miners.
newsitem.headline: Tremors hamper rescue of Peruvian miners.

text.p: Rescue efforts to free at least two miners trapped inside a collapsed tunnel were hampered on Sunday by persistent tremors, five days after an earthquake that struck southern Peru.

"The latest information is that they are still alive. But there are so many tremors. And every tremor causes a landslide that just puts us back to square one," said Flora Valenzuela, Civil Defence spokeswoman in Lima.

Digging with picks and shovels since Thursday, firefighters and miners have tried to reach the men stuck inside a hillside gold mine at Guanillo near Nazca, 290 miles (460 km) to the south of the capital Lima.

They were believed to have survived underground due to small rations of food and water they took into the tunnels Tuesday. Experts estimated the men would survive only three The quake that shook southern Peru Tuesday and rocked Lima for a minute measured 6.4 on the Richter scale. It killed 14 people, injured hundreds and left tens of thousands homeless.
The quake killed one miner at Moyohauca, 375 miles (600 km) south of Lima, in the department of Arequipa, and tens more had to be dragged out of several remote mines around Nazca.
